key_decisions: Chose the DERIVED fix over baking sam3 into the Pod image. Baking is what the design documented and is a one-line Dockerfile edit, but it costs +1.75GB on every image pull forever, a dev build on BOTH legs (MPI-340), a POD_IMAGE_VERSION_DEV bump and an app restart - and the next engineAsset repeats all of it, so the bug class survives. Volume-installing makes remote derive from DEPS exactly as local does. The user approved this explicitly after being shown both.

UNFLAGGED is the safe default for `bakedOnPod`. A missing flag costs a volume download; a WRONG flag makes a weight unreachable on remote and the failure is a 503 mid-generation on a billed Pod, not a build error. The legend in assetDeps.js says this, and the lockstep test enforces it against the real Dockerfile.

Reused the ordinary remote install path rather than writing new install machinery. It already owns the volume pre-check and dedupe (warm volume = no-op), the serial chain that stops a CPU Pod being starved by parallel aria2c jobs, and SSE/stall reporting. Job id `engine:assets` is namespaced like `plugin:<id>` so it cannot collide with a model id, and no consumer renders a card for an unknown id, so the heal is silent by construction.

Install is eager on connect, NOT lazy/on-demand: local installs engine assets WITH the engine, and a masking click that stalls for a 1.75GB fetch is worse than a connect that fetches once and is warm after.
The sweep was NOT run for 4 of 6 items. The user chose fix-first so one Pod session clears all six, which is the entire reason the MPI-385 umbrella exists.
